title: Affordable housing and fire station at 450-470 King Street East
subtitle: Dundee Secondary Plan referred to June 29 for more talks with developers on parkland, heritage and worship space.
overview: The committee recommended rezoning 450-470 King Street East to allow a 19-storey mixed-use building {{vote:m1}}. The city-owned site would hold about 280 affordable rental units, a new downtown fire station, community space and a public plaza. It would have no resident parking. Because this is a committee, the recommendation goes to a Special Council Meeting on June 1, 2026. The committee also recommended endorsing the urban design report for use in site plan approval.

Delegates opposed the residential component. They asked for a park instead, citing the neighbourhood's shortage of parkland, and raised concerns about density, parking and construction timelines. Staff said the funding used to buy the land requires it to go to housing. Staff also said a separate parkland acquisition strategy will prioritize King East.

On the Dundee Secondary Plan for new southwest Kitchener neighbourhoods, the committee referred the staff recommendation to the June 29, 2026 Council meeting {{vote:m2}}. This gives staff time to speak further with developers and delegates about their concerns. Those concerns include whether trails count toward parkland dedication and how a heritage property is shown on the plan.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the zoning change from SGA 2 to SGA 3, with site-specific provisions capping height at 19 storeys, for the affordable housing and fire station project.
The committee recommended endorsing the Urban Design Report and directing staff to carry it out through the future site plan approval process.
The committee referred the recommended Official Plan Amendment for the Dundee Secondary Plan to the June 29, 2026 Council meeting so staff can engage further with developers and delegates.
The referred recommendation includes receiving the draft final Class Environmental Assessment and filing it with the Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks for the 30-day review.

debate: Delegates opposed to the King Street East project asked that the land become a park. They said King East has one of the city's largest parkland shortages and that the plaza is not a substitute. Staff replied that the funding behind the land purchase requires housing, so the land cannot be repurposed as a park.

Some delegates and councillors were concerned about the jump from the eight-storey zoning, and from the earlier proposal, to 19 storeys. Staff and the applicant said the Official Plan already permits taller buildings here, and that the larger site and the funding model made the extra height necessary to lower per-unit costs.

Parking drew repeated concern, especially for visitors and for service providers who would visit the building. Supporters said the site is near LRT and transit and that most tenants will come from a waiting list and may not own vehicles. Some councillors said the nearby market garage should be considered during site plan review.

On the Dundee plan, a landowner's planner said trails should keep counting toward parkland dedication, and a second delegate wanted a farmhouse removed from the heritage mapping. Another delegate said commercial space should be spread more evenly. Staff said parkland credit should favour programmable park space, and that the farmhouse is not designated but is shown because of its heritage value.

Councillors asked how places of worship would find land in the new community. Staff said such uses are permitted in most land use designations and that staff have connected faith communities with landowners. One councillor wanted more certainty than competing with commercial uses.
